Rice University, Houston, TX, USA

      Abstract
The standard approach to algorithm development is to focus on a specific problem and develop for it
a specific algorithm. Codd’s introduction of the relational model in 1970 included two fundamental
ideas: (1) Relations provide a universal data representation formalism, and (2) Relational databases
can be queried using first-order logic. Realizing these ideas required the development of a meta-
algorithm, which takes a declarative query and executes it with respect to a database. In this talk, I
will describe this approach, which I call Logical Algorithmics, in detail, and explore its profound
ramification.
